plan: Store the workspace as a single deep-copied dict tree; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.

Implement one recursive generator (_walk) over item lists and reuse it for word counting, marker collection, and containment checks; dispatch on the 'kind' field to handle note vs reference contributions.
Count note words by first stripping [[?identifier]] markers with a regex, then counting \b\w+\b runs; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers from both note-text markers and reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted.
Render the outline by depth-first traversal, emitting the workspace title then '  '*depth + 'kind: title' per item.

Implement move() as validate-before-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group), reject non-containers, reject destinations inside the moved item's subtree via an id set, and bounds-check the index — all before any mutation, so failed moves leave the tree untouched. Then pop from the source list and append/insert into the destination.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at construction and export (copy.deepcopy in __init__ and to_data)
Recursive generator traversal (_walk) shared by all tree-wide queries
Kind-based dispatch distinguishing note, reference, and container behavior
Regex marker stripping before regex word counting so identifiers never count as words
Set-union plus sorted() for deduplicated lexicographic marker output
Depth-first outline rendering with two-space-per-level indentation
Validate-before-mutate move protocol guaranteeing failed moves leave state unchanged
Id-set subtree containment check to reject self/descendant destinations
Insertion-index bounds validation (0..len inclusive) against the destination before removal
